key_insight: lPINN shifts most learning offline by pretraining a differentiable neural basis, then solves each new PDE instance online with only a linear output layer constrained by physics.
engineering_relevance: This can cut inference cost dramatically while improving accuracy for forward and inverse PDE problems, making it attractive for fast scientific simulation and parameter estimation.
method: Learn continuous operator-compatible basis functions from an ensemble of numerical solutions using data plus derivatives or physics residuals.
Freeze the pretrained nonlinear hidden layers for new problems and optimize only the final linear layer under governing-equation, boundary/initial, regularization, and observation losses.
Use automatic differentiation so the learned basis remains differentiable and can be evaluated on finer meshes without retraining.
evidence_signal: The paper reports tests on advection-diffusion, Burgers', and nonlinear pendulum problems, with lower solution/parameter errors than vanilla PINNs and online speedups from about 10x to over 1000x, especially with limited residual or measurement data.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the offline training ensemble, so extrapolation to poorly represented regimes may be less reliable.
paper_title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers
